title: Exploring the English-Speaking World
summary: Explore traditions, customs, landmarks and ways of life in different English-speaking countries.
keyIdeas: English is spoken in diverse countries, including the UK, USA, Ireland, Canada and Australia.
Countries can share or adapt celebrations. Thanksgiving is celebrated on different dates in the USA and Canada.
Learning about cultures and polite behaviour helps us treat others with respect and empathy.

activities.prompt: In many primary schools across the United Kingdom, children wear a school uniform every school day.
activities.explanation: True. Many British schools use uniforms, but rules vary between schools.
activities.hint: Think about descriptions of British schools in stories or films.

activities.prompt: Many families in the United States gather on the fourth Thursday of November for a special meal and to give thanks. What is the celebration called?
activities.explanation: Thanksgiving is celebrated in the USA in November. A traditional meal can include turkey and pumpkin pie.
activities.hint: The name includes the idea of giving thanks.

activities.prompt: Sort these celebrations by the country they are associated with in this activity.
activities.explanation: November's Thanksgiving is associated with the USA; Canada's is in October. Bonfire Night and Scotland's St Andrew's Day are associated here with the UK.
activities.hint: Bonfire Night remembers the Gunpowder Plot in London in 1605.

items.text: Thanksgiving on the fourth Thursday of November

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence about a popular British drink.
activities.explanation: Many people in the UK enjoy tea, sometimes with milk and biscuits. Customs and preferences vary.
activities.hint: Choose the drink made by infusing tea leaves.
activities.sentence: In the United Kingdom, many people enjoy having hot ___ with milk in the afternoon.

activities.prompt: Aisha's pen pal Liam lives in Sydney, Australia. He writes, 'On Christmas Day, my family goes to the beach and has a barbecue!'. Why is December a summer month in Sydney?
activities.explanation: Australia is in the Southern Hemisphere, so its seasons are opposite to Europe's. December is a summer month there, although weather varies.
activities.hint: Compare seasons in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
options: Because Australians move Christmas celebrations to August.
Because Australia has no winter anywhere in the country.
Because Australia is in the Southern Hemisphere, where December is summer.

activities.prompt: A school invents these Pancake Day race rules: prepare, start running, flip three times on the track, then finish. Put the rules in order.
activities.explanation: This is an invented school race. Some communities hold pancake races, but their rules can differ.
activities.hint: Prepare with the pan first and cross the finish line last.
items: Put on an apron and hold a frying pan with a pancake.
Run along the designated track when the whistle blows.
Toss and flip the pancake in the air at least three times.
Cross the finish line with the pancake still inside the pan.

activities.prompt: Sort these vocabulary choices by their typical association in this comparison. Both varieties also share words.
activities.explanation: Here, 'autumn' and 'holiday' are associated with British English; 'fall' and 'vacation' with American English. These are tendencies, not exclusive boundaries: 'cookie' is also used in the UK.

activities.prompt: Lucía sees a 'Stand on the right' sign on a Tube escalator. Which action follows the sign?
activities.explanation: The sign tells her to stand on the right, leaving the left side clear.
activities.hint: Read which side the sign names.
options: Stand on the right side so people in a hurry can walk on the left.
Stand in the middle with your bags to block both sides.
Sit on the moving steps while the escalator goes down.
